Security lead requested SOC2/ISO evidence and KMS integration details. Next: send pricing, benchmarks, and schedule pilot kickoff.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Ortiz (Redwood AE); Marcus Lee (Redwood SE); Priya Sharma (Lumen Head of ML); Dan Keegan (CTO); Aisha Morgan (Security); Leo Park (SRE)
---
[00:00] Jenna Ortiz: hey everyone, um thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro then jump into the console walkthrough, i'm jenna from Redwood, role AE, with Marcus our SE.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: hi all, excited to show the usage analytics and per-route views, i'll drive the demo, jenna will chime on pricing and commercial stuff.
[00:20] Priya Sharma: thanks, quick context - we're looking at embedding LLM features across patient support and clinician tools, privacy's a big one for us, plus cost predictability, so per-route cost is super relevant.
[00:35] Dan Keegan: timeline is tight, want pilot in next 2-3 weeks if vendor checks out.
[00:42] Jenna Ortiz: great, we'll highlight the pilot flow and metrics you can see in console.
[01:10] Marcus Lee: opening the console now, shared screen (link: https://redwood.app/console/demo/usage-123) - top-level overview shows token volume, avg latency, and per-model spend across the last 30 days. you can filter by route, model, and time window.
[01:32] Marcus Lee: notice the per-route pie chart - here 'patient-chat' route accounts for 62% of token spend, despite being 45% of calls, that's because avg tokens per session is higher.
[01:55] Priya Sharma: can you break down prompt vs completion tokens per route?
[02:05] Marcus Lee: yep, clicking into the route - you get tokens by direction (prompt/completion), and a tied cost column that attributes unit cost per token depending on model variant. sometimes transcription shows Redwood model names as 'RWood-v2' in our analytics export - ignore that it's mapping to actual model ids.
[02:40] Leo Park: is the cost calc using current pricing or projected reserved pricing?
[02:46] Jenna Ortiz: console defaults to hosted list pricing; for Dedicated or Reserved we can upload your commit and the cost dashboard will show effective unit prices and savings.
[03:05] Marcus Lee: showing the per-route latency distribution - p50/p95/p99. you can set alerts on p95 or on sudden token spikes.
[03:30] Aisha Morgan: on security, do logs contain PHI? how redacted are traces?
[03:38] Marcus Lee: by default logs are metadata only, full message logs are opt-in and you can configure retention and redaction. for Private deployments you control the control plane and KMS integration - keys never leave your cloud.
[04:05] Aisha Morgan: we need SOC2 and ISO artifacts plus KMS/HSM integration details.
[04:12] Jenna Ortiz: noted - i'll attach SOC2 pack and our security whitepaper; Marcus will include KMS integration doc.
[04:29] Dan Keegan: curious about per-route cost forecasting - can we project monthly spend if volumes change?
[04:36] Marcus Lee: yes, the console has a forecast view: you set expected qps/avg token and it projects cost per route. also shows sensitivity to model switches (e.g., gpt-like vs quantized open models).
[05:05] Priya Sharma: about model pinning - we need deterministic outputs for certain clinical routes. can we pin model versions per-route and lock rollouts?
[05:15] Marcus Lee: absolutely - per-route config supports model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to lower-cost variants on high load. you'll see rollout history and percent traffic in the dashboard.
[05:45] Marcus Lee: switching to cost breakdown tab, here's token-level cost + amortized infra overhead for a Dedicated pool. note how batching and KV cache reduce effective tokens billed for repeated prefixes.
[06:10] Jenna Ortiz: an important lever is prefix caching - for patient templates you'll often hit cache hits and cost drops significantly. we can show estimated savings for your real prompt sets during the pilot.
[06:40] Priya Sharma: that sounds promising. can you run an initial estimate for our 'patient-summary' prompt set?
[06:47] Marcus Lee: yes, if you share sample prompts and avg session counts we'll run a benchmark and return a savings projection.
[07:10] Marcus Lee: small transcription glitch - sometimes the console exports model id as 'redwood_ded' in CSVs, it's just a naming artifact.
[07:30] Leo Park: any integrations for our observability stack (Datadog / NewRelic)?
[07:36] Marcus Lee: we have tracing hooks and export connectors, plus an API to pull per-route metrics into your observability pipeline.
[08:05] Dan Keegan: on latency - for clinician-facing flows we need p95 under 400ms, is that realistic on hosted? dedicated?
[08:15] Marcus Lee: depends on model variant and sequence length; hosted with smaller quantized models can hit that, Dedicated gives more consistent p95 under SLA. Private on-prem gives the tightest control if you co-locate near your app.
[08:45] Priya Sharma: what's the expected cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
[08:52] Jenna Ortiz: rough ballpark: Dedicated reserved commit can reduce per-token infra cost by 20-40% depending on utilization and batching. total customer price will factor in commit term and support add-ons. i'll include modeled examples in the deck.
[09:20] Marcus Lee: showing the 'anomaly detection' card - flags when per-route cost deviates vs baseline. useful for spotting runaway prompts.
[09:35] Priya Sharma: do you support anonymization/redaction pipelines pre-ingest?
[09:41] Marcus Lee: yes we have ingestion hooks so you can run a pre-processor lambda to scrub PHI before tokens hit Redwood. for Private we can do this inside your VPC.
[10:05] Aisha Morgan: about audit logs and retention, we need 7 years for some flows - does Redwood support long-term retention?
[10:14] Jenna Ortiz: yes, audit logs retention is configurable; for long term you can forward logs to your S3/GCS bucket. note there may be cost for long term storage.
[10:40] Marcus Lee: jumping to per-route chargeback - this view lets you export CSV per team/route, includes token counts, model used, avg latency, and cost. you can also map routes to cost centers.
[11:05] Dan Keegan: that's helpful for internal chargeback.
[11:12] Marcus Lee: demoing a sample export (link: export.csv) - the CSV shows token split by prompt/completion but sometimes proper nouns in prompts are redacted in the export depending on settings.
[11:45] Priya Sharma: can the console show model quality regressions over time? we want to tie evals to production traffic.
[11:53] Marcus Lee: yes, the Optimize integration ties eval sets to routes and surfaces regressions with example prompts causing differences. you can set threshold alerts.
[12:20] Marcus Lee: quick aside - if you plan to use embeddings heavily across search, the console also tracks embedding units and cost per embedding.
[12:40] Priya Sharma: for patient search we will, yep. how do you price embeddings vs text gen?
[12:47] Jenna Ortiz: embeddings are usually priced per unit (vector) and are separate meter from token gen; we'll show your estimated monthly in the pricing model.
[13:10] Leo Park: about network egress for Private deployments, any recommendations?
[13:16] Marcus Lee: keep models and inference in same region; for on-prem we recommend colocated infra. we document bandwidth requirements in the deployment guide.
[13:40] Dan Keegan: can we run a quick scenario - 200 qps on patient-chat with avg 300 tokens in, 500 tokens out - what would console show?
[13:50] Marcus Lee: pulling up forecast mode, projecting monthly tokens and cost; toggling between a quantized open model and a larger hosted model shows ~35% cost delta and latency differences at p95.
[14:20] Priya Sharma: one risk is hallucination in clinician summaries, do you have guardrails?
[14:28] Marcus Lee: Optimize has quality monitors and we can run rerankers / verification steps; also you can send a verification prompt to a specialized model before committing to the final summary.
[14:55] Aisha Morgan: do you have a data residency story for EU patients?
[15:03] Jenna Ortiz: yes, we support region routing and private VPC deployments; for regulated flows we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS so keys and data remain in-region.
[15:30] Marcus Lee: showing rollout tab again - you can schedule a canary and monitor per-route metrics live. if quality drops the system can auto-roll back.
[16:00] Marcus Lee: switching to billing modeling - console will let you model Reserved capacity pricing, show amortized infra costs, and simulate burst capacity.
[16:30] Dan Keegan: curious about how batching logic affects latency observed in console - do you show batching windows?
[16:39] Marcus Lee: yes, we surface average batch sizes and the latency contribution per batching window; console annotates when batching thresholds change due to traffic.
[17:05] Priya Sharma: talking about prefix caching earlier - can you show an example where cache hit rate reduces cost?
[17:12] Marcus Lee: here's a route with 70% cache hit - effective per-call token cost dropped 40% after enabling caching and short TTL for KV.
[17:40] Leo Park: do we need SDK changes to leverage cache?
[17:45] Marcus Lee: minor SDK changes - we provide docs and code snippets; for many clients it's a header and enabling cache on the route.
[18:10] Jenna Ortiz: at this point i want to recap commercial options: hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved commits, and Private deployments. each has tradeoffs on cost, latency, and compliance.
[18:28] Dan Keegan: for Lumen Health I'm leaning Dedicated for predictable costs, but want a pilot on Hosted to validate quality.
[18:38] Jenna Ortiz: we typically do a 4-6 week pilot on hosted with sample traffic, run the benchmark, then move to Dedicated if looks good.
[19:00] Marcus Lee: next steps for pilot - Marcus will request sample prompt sets and a small S3 bucket with anonymized logs; we'll run a benchmark and return a cost/latency report.
[19:18] Priya Sharma: timeline works.
[19:25] Aisha Morgan: reminder - need security artifacts before pilot kickoff.
[19:30] Jenna Ortiz: will send SOC2 and KMS docs.
[19:40] Marcus Lee: minor note: console export sometimes misspells route names if teams rename them quickly, just a small UX quirk.
[20:05] Marcus Lee: opening the 'alerts and policies' workflow - you can create routes-level SLOs and auto actions like throttling or route fallback to lower-cost model.
[20:35] Dan Keegan: can the fallback be region-aware? we have some EU traffic that must stay in EU region.
[20:42] Marcus Lee: yes, routing policies respect region constraints and won't fallback outside allowed regions.
[21:05] Priya Sharma: can we get a demo export for our team to play with?
[21:10] Jenna Ortiz: we'll provide a demo dataset and console URL; Marcus will share sample creds with restricted read-only access.
[21:40] Jenna Ortiz: quick Q - any major blockers you're thinking of?
[21:45] Dan Keegan: main blockers: security artifacts, confirming cost model, and pilot alignment with clinical QA.
[21:52] Priya Sharma: also want clear success criteria for accuracy and latency.
[22:05] Marcus Lee: we'll include a success criteria template with the pilot materials.
[22:30] Marcus Lee: final demo bits - showing Optimize's prompt regression graphs tied to routes; you can annotate problematic prompts and trigger re-evals.
[23:00] Aisha Morgan: ok that's useful. can you confirm whether logs can be stored in our S3 with encryption keys managed by us?
[23:08] Marcus Lee: yes, for Private and Dedicated you can forward logs to your S3 under your KMS key; hosted has a managed option but we can also set up log forwarding.
[23:40] Jenna Ortiz: i'm going to capture next steps - will send pricing, pilot agreement, SOC2 + KMS docs, and Marcus will request sample prompts and logs.
[24:00] Jenna Ortiz: any other questions?
[24:05] Leo Park: none from me.
[24:10] Priya Sharma: all good.
[24:15] Dan Keegan: thanks, appreciate the detail.
[24:20] Jenna Ortiz: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and next actions.
---
End of recording (approx 55 mins).

Notes: transcription contains small naming inconsistencies (RWood-v2, redwood_ded) and occasional mis-attributions typical of automated calls. Shared artifacts referenced during call: Deck (https://redwood.com/deck/usage-analytics), Benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared via drive), Demo console link (https://redwood.app/console/demo/usage-123).
